summary: Seek out kuay jub (ก๋วยจั๊บ) in Yaowarat: rolled rice-noodle sheets curl into chewy tubes in a peppery pork broth, often served with crispy pork, boiled egg and offal. Michelin highlights Nai Ek Roll Noodles for its thicker noodles, while Guay Jub Ouan Pochana is known for a clear-broth style. This is a flexible meal stop rather than a fixed attraction; check the chosen stall's current schedule and menu before going.
whyGo: The rolled rice noodles have a distinctive springy texture unlike the flat noodles common in other Thai soups.
White pepper gives the broth a warming, aromatic kick; crispy pork adds crunch.
Yaowarat has several well-known versions, so it can anchor a casual Chinatown food walk.
bestFor: Noodle and pork fans curious about Thai-Chinese food
Visitors comfortable eating in busy Chinatown shopfronts
A hearty meal between Yaowarat sights or during an evening food crawl
skipIf: You avoid pork, offal or animal-based broths
You need a reliably mild dish or strict allergen control without checking ingredients directly
Crowded, compact dining spaces or uncertain step-free access are unsuitable
duration: Allow about 45–90 minutes for a bowl and a short wander; this is a planning estimate, with queues and the wider food crawl affecting the visit.
cost: No current price for a bowl was verified. Allow roughly THB 100–200 per person as a planning estimate for a bowl and drink; confirm menu prices and extras at the stall.
hours: Michelin's Yaowarat guide reports Nai Ek Roll Noodles open daily 09:00–00:00. Hours can change, and other kuay jub shops differ; check the named venue close to your visit.
bestTime: For a quieter meal, try before the dinner rush; the dish also works as a daytime lunch at Nai Ek according to Michelin. Evening is livelier for a broader Yaowarat street-food walk.
gettingThere: Take the MRT Blue Line to Wat Mangkon, a convenient gateway to Yaowarat, then walk to the selected shop. Nai Ek Roll Noodles is at 442 Soi Yaowarat 9; use a current map for the exact route. The MRT operator lists daily service from 06:00 to midnight.
booking: Treat this as a casual walk-in meal. Michelin lists Nai Ek as a shop serving throughout the day; no reservation information was found. Expect possible queues at popular times.
accessibility: Step-free routes, accessible toilets, table clearance and seating at individual stalls were not verified. Yaowarat sidewalks and shopfront dining may be crowded; contact a chosen venue if access needs are essential.
practicalTips: Ask for kuay jub (ก๋วยจั๊บ); versions differ, including clear broth and darker, denser broth.
Some bowls include pork offal, crispy pork and egg. Michelin says Guay Jub Mr. Jo can be ordered with or without offal, but confirm ingredients at any specific shop.
Pepper heat is a defining feature, so ask whether the broth can be made milder if needed.
Ask staff about fish sauce, soy, other allergens and cross-contact; recipes vary. Carry cash as a backup.
decemberNotes: Kuay jub is a year-round dish, with no seasonal December 2026 schedule found. Check individual holiday hours, especially around Christmas and New Year; Yaowarat can be busy in the evening.
uncertainties: Current menu prices, payment options and December 2026 holiday hours were not confirmed with a restaurant.
Opening times in published guides can change; verify the chosen shop before travelling.
Broth, pork cuts, spice level, allergens and access conditions vary by vendor.
